<!-- pr-reviewer: 203d87bcede99c7de7a8744231c076d5a997e922 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review, because the PR changes posted G-code.

## What looks good

- The guard is a visible refusal by name. It obeys the Prime Directive, and issue #2683 permits a refusal as a correct answer.
- The guard is the same block in `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1403-1419` and `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:1032-1048`.
- The register number is correct for each system: 5210 + 20 x the system number gives `#5230` for G54 and `#5330` for G59.
- The guard uses `nextO()`, so its O-number does not collide with a tolerance test.
- `wcsIndex` in `linuxcnc.cps` changes only in `offsetWord`, and only the `WorkOffset` PARAM calls that function.
- A Z-only result and a measure-only result have no guard.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2683-probe-rotated-wcs.md` gives the algebra, the dropped options and the cost of a later change.
- The new test file is in `crates/post/tests/`, imports only `camcraft_post`, and has a provenance line and a Gate map.
- The body has `Changelog:`, `Effort:` and `Fixes #2683`. The commit subject is conventional.

## Goldens, read line by line

Six goldens changed. Each one has the same four added lines directly before its `G10 L20` line. No other line changed (24 insertions, 0 deletions).

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_edge.nc`: `o902`, X only.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_corner.nc`: `o903`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_bore_centre.nc`: `o903`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_boss_centre.nc`: `o903`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_bore_centre_mm.nc`: `o903`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/probe.nc`: `o903`.

Each guard tests `[[#5230 NE 0] OR [#5250 NE 0]]`. That agrees with a probe in G54 that sets G55 (`P2`).

## Results merged with main

Built and tested locally, trial-merged with `upstream/main` at `75e74a9cb`. The merge was clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-fail-fast` | 94 binaries ok, 776 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored |
| `probe_rotated_wcs` | 5 passed |
| `probe_tormach` (reads five of the moved goldens) | 7 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Mutations that I ran again:

- `if (xy)` changed to `if (true)` in `linuxcnc.cps`: `a_z_only_result_and_a_measure_only_result_have_no_guard` red.
- `20 * tgt` changed to `20 * wcsIndex` in `tormach.cps` (the target register is not tested): `setting_another_offset_stops_when_either_is_rotated` and `the_guard_is_written_once_under_its_own_o_number` red, and five golden tests of `probe_tormach` red.
- The two files restored: `probe_rotated_wcs` 5 passed, `probe_tormach` 7 passed.

Not run:

- The app suites. No Rust file of `crates/app` changed, and the tests of `camcraft-post` read the moved app goldens. The only app test that reads a `G10 L20` line (`crates/app/tests/probe_op.rs:295`) uses a Z-only result, which has no guard.
- No program ran on a control. The PR body says the same.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1416` and `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:1045`: if `SetWorkOffset` + 1 is more than 9, `workOffsetName(tgt)` gives an empty string and the message ends with `OR `. The `G10 L20 P<n>` line had the same limit before this PR. A follow-up issue (`P7`) can refuse such a target by name.
2. The guard also stops a program when the two rotations are equal. The decision file says how to relax it after a run on LinuxCNC or PathPilot. That run is still open work.
3. The words `NE`, `OR` and the parameters `#5230`.. agree with the LinuxCNC G-code reference as I know it. I did not open the reference during this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Merge class: SAME. The reviewed head is the merged head, `203d87bcede99c7de7a8744231c076d5a997e922`. No commit came after it.

This merge relies on the safety-tier review by mkinney's review agent of 07:21 UTC on that head. The PR fixes a P3 (#2683) and touches no P1, so no second review is necessary.
